node.label: Rainfall, monsoon & climate drivers
node.summary: Rainfall deficits and drivers like El Nino and the Indian Ocean Dipole.

facts.text: Meghalaya got only **38.3 mm** of rain in October against a normal of 255 mm, an **85%** deficit; the monsoon deficit was 60%.
facts.plain: Meghalaya got only 38.3 mm of rain in October against a normal of 255 mm, an 85% deficit; the monsoon deficit was 60%.

facts.text: India's 2026 southwest monsoon ended nearly **13% below the long-term average** (87 cm) — the driest season on record (since 1901) for East and Northeast India — despite IMD's April forecast of 92% of the Long Period Average; of seven Indian monsoons since 1950 that coincided with a moderate/strong El Nino, five (including 2026) saw rainfall at least 10% below average, while 1997 was a rare exception because a favourable Indian Ocean Dipole phase offset El Nino's effect; the monsoon supplies about three-quarters of India's annual rainfall and roughly 40% of farmland remains unirrigated.
